nativeBarcodeDialog.description: This run folder holds more than one MinKNOW native barcode. A run scores one plate, and its native barcodes are replicates of that plate: each selected barcode is demultiplexed on its own, and the pipeline then picks the best replicate per variant. Cancel stops the analysis.

parameters.subtitle: Thresholds and ingest mode for this batch.
parameters.targetAmpliconLengthHelp: Expected amplicon length after barcode sorting. Leave blank to auto-detect from sample reads; set manually when the distribution is noisy.

parameters.minQscoreHelp: Minimum per-read qscore threshold when sequencing_summary metadata is available.
parameters.normalizeHeadersHelp: Writes the well name into FASTA headers instead of preserving ONT read IDs. This makes downstream per-well parsing more consistent.
parameters.rawRunOptionsAriaLabel: Raw run demux and filter options
parameters.barcodeRunsAutomatically: Barcode sorting runs automatically when you press the main Run button.
parameters.cdsStartHelp: 0-based CDS start offset used when translating consensus sequence to amino acids. If the reference file has CDS annotations, select a detected candidate.

parameters.manyCutoff: Max unexpected AA changes per well
parameters.manyCutoffHelp: Wells with more amino-acid changes than this threshold are flagged as MANY (low-confidence, unpickable).
parameters.maxConsensusNFractionHelp: Maximum fraction of ambiguous N bases tolerated in a well consensus before it is rejected (0.0 to 1.0). Default 0.0 rejects any consensus containing an N; higher values allow more ambiguity.
parameters.bimodalTooltip: Distribution looks bimodal. Recommended uses knee detection.
parameters.normalizeHeadersAriaLabel: Write well name as FASTA header instead of ONT read ID
parameters.legacyKbCutoffAriaLabel: Legacy min file size KB cutoff (proxy for read depth)

parameters.modeAmpliconTitle: Linear PCR amplicon target. Reads cover a single defined region; consensus called per barcode within that region.
parameters.modePlasmidTitle: Circular plasmid target. Reads can wrap the origin; consensus accounts for full plasmid topology.
parameters.ingestBarcodeTitle: Group reads by Nanopore barcode (NB01, NB02, ...). Each barcode bin becomes one sample.
parameters.ingestAmpliconTitle: Group reads by amplicon identity. Use when multiple amplicons share a barcode or when demultiplexing by sequence match.

parameters.inputModeSortedBarcodeTitle: Start from already-sorted barcode directories (fastq.gz per barcode). Skips MinKNOW sorting; runs consensus calling.
parameters.inputModeRawRunTitle: Start from a raw MinKNOW run folder (fastq_pass/ + run metadata). Full pipeline: sort barcodes, filter, then consensus.
parameters.minFilteredDepthHelp: Cutoff based on read count passing the length-window filter. This is the primary depth-based quality cutoff.
parameters.minFilteredDepthAria: Min filtered depth (reads). Length-window-filtered read count cutoff.
parameters.minFilteredDepthTitle: Primary depth cutoff. Based on reads passing the length-window filter.

parameters.legacyKbHelp: Legacy cutoff using FASTA file size as a proxy for read depth. Affected by compression ratio, length distribution, and library variation.
parameters.legacyKbTooltip: File-size-based proxy cutoff. Affected by compression ratio, length distribution, and library variation. Use as reference only.
parameters.modeHelp: Analysis mode: amplicon (linear PCR product) or plasmid (circular). Choose plasmid for whole-vector consensus.
parameters.ingestHelp: Ingest layout: barcode (per-well demultiplexed) or amplicon (single bulk read set).
parameters.inputSourceHelp: Input source: consensus (pre-called), sorted_barcode (per-well FASTQ), or raw_run (MinKNOW run folder).

barcodeSetup.title: Barcode Package Setup
barcodeSetup.subtitle: Generate a MAME barcode package from a CDS FASTA and barcode seed file.
barcodeSetup.outputLocationHelper: Folder where the barcode package files are written. Leave empty to use the project's design/ folder.
barcodeSetup.cdsFastaHelper: Plasmid or construct map (GenBank or SnapGene .dna) containing the gene plus flanking template on both sides. MAME primers bind outside the gene, so at least flank_max (default 400 bp) of template is needed on each side. A CDS-only FASTA will not work. gene_start / gene_end are 0-based indices into this sequence.

barcodeSetup.cdsCandidateHelp: CDS candidate auto-detected from the FASTA. Coordinates apply on selection.
barcodeSetup.geneNameHelp: Short gene identifier used in output filenames and labels (e.g. egfp).

barcodeSetup.bindingMaxLenHelp: Maximum primer binding length (nt). Above 35 increases secondary structure risk.

readCount.what: Reads that passed the alignment filters and fed the consensus pileup for this well, read from the depth=N header of the consensus FASTA.
readCount.stage: Consensus calling, after the MAPQ and span filters.
readCount.effect: Gates the verdict. Below the depth floor the well is LOWDEPTH and no further check runs. A well with mixed positions whose depth sits below the mixed-call floor is also reported LOWDEPTH rather than MIXED, because a second allele cannot be told apart from sequencing error there.
readCount.thresholdDepthOff: The read-depth gate was disabled for this run.
readCount.thresholdMixed: A confident MIXED call needs {{count}} reads or more (the depth floor times {{factor}}).
readCount.thresholdMixedOff: No mixed-call depth floor, because the read-depth gate was disabled.
readCount.thresholdFileSize: Wells that carry no depth header at all fall back to a consensus file size of {{size}} KB.

inputReads.what: Reads assigned to this well before alignment.
inputReads.stage: Barcode demultiplexing, before alignment. Empty when the run was analyzed from consensus FASTA instead of raw reads.
inputReads.effect: Diagnostic only. No gate reads this number. Compare it with the aligned and filtered counts to see where reads were lost.

alignedReads.what: Reads that produced at least one alignment to the reference, counted before the MAPQ and span filters.
alignedReads.stage: Alignment, before filtering. Empty when the run was analyzed from consensus FASTA instead of raw reads.
alignedReads.effect: Diagnostic only. No gate reads this number. A large drop from the input reads points at the wrong reference or at off-target material in the well.

mapqFailed.what: Reads dropped because their alignment did not reach the mapping-quality (MAPQ) floor.
mapqFailed.stage: Alignment filtering, between the aligned count and the filtered read count. Zero when the run was analyzed from consensus FASTA.
mapqFailed.effect: Diagnostic only. No gate reads this number. A high count means the reads map ambiguously, typically a repeat or the wrong reference.

spanFailed.what: Reads dropped because their alignment does not cover the full reference length.
spanFailed.stage: Alignment filtering, applied after the MAPQ filter. Zero when the run was analyzed from consensus FASTA.
spanFailed.effect: Diagnostic only. No gate reads this number. A high count usually means truncated reads or an amplicon shorter than the reference.

mixedPositions.what: Positions where a second A/C/G/T base rises above the minor-allele threshold at sufficient pileup depth. A 51/49 well looks exact in the majority consensus and this is what exposes it.
mixedPositions.stage: Consensus calling, from the per-position pileup.
mixedPositions.effect: Gates the verdict. Any count above zero makes the well MIXED, unless depth sits below the mixed-call floor, in which case LOWDEPTH is reported instead.
mixedPositions.thresholdDepth: MIXED is reported only at {{count}} reads or more; below that the well is LOWDEPTH.
mixedPositions.thresholdDepthOff: No mixed-call depth floor, because the read-depth gate was disabled for this run.

maxMinorAllele.what: The largest second-base fraction across all positions in this well, that is, the single noisiest position.
maxMinorAllele.stage: Consensus calling, from the per-position pileup.
maxMinorAllele.effect: Diagnostic only. No gate reads this number directly; the mixed-position count above is what the MIXED gate uses. Read it as the size of the strongest competing signal.
maxMinorAllele.noiseFloor: An ordinary position in this well sits at {{value}} (median). A maximum near that median is background; one far above it is a real second allele.
maxMinorAllele.noiseFloorUnknown: This run reported no median minor-allele fraction, so there is no noise floor to read the maximum against.

lowDepthPositions.what: Reference positions whose pileup depth stayed below the minimum, so no base could be called from reads there.
lowDepthPositions.stage: Consensus calling, from the per-position pileup.
lowDepthPositions.effect: Diagnostic only. No gate reads this number. It is reported next to a NO_CALL verdict to show the ambiguity came from missing coverage rather than from poor reads.

consensusN.what: Share of covered consensus positions emitted as N (no call). Numerator and denominator both range over positions the reads reached, so reference positions never read do not dilute it.
consensusN.stage: Consensus calling, after the majority vote.
consensusN.effect: Gates the verdict. Above the ceiling the well is NO_CALL and its amino-acid calls are not trusted. Distinct from LOWDEPTH: depth can be ample while the consensus is still dominated by no-call bases.
consensusN.thresholdOff: The N-fraction gate was disabled for this run.
consensusN.notEvaluable: This consensus file carries no covered-scoped N fraction, so the value shown is a substituted 0.0 and the NO_CALL gate was skipped. Re-run consensus calling to restore it.
consensusN.evaluableUnknown: This result was saved before the run reported whether the N fraction could be evaluated, so whether the NO_CALL gate ran is unknown.

lowQualityBases.what: Individual base calls excluded from the pileup vote because their FASTQ quality was below the minimum.
lowQualityBases.stage: Consensus calling, while the pileup is accumulated. Zero for inputs that carry no quality scores, such as FASTA-only consensus files.
lowQualityBases.effect: Diagnostic only. No gate reads this number. It is reported next to a NO_CALL verdict to show the ambiguity came from base quality rather than from missing coverage.

parameterPanel.title: Parameters
parameterPanel.strategyHint_partial: Forward and reverse are independent with overlap upstream of the codon.
parameterPanel.strategyHint_full: Reverse = rc(forward). Single primer Tm and length apply to both.
parameterPanel.strategyHelp:
Partial (Gibson): overlap upstream of the codon; fwd and rev are independent.
Full (Q5 SDM): rev = rc(fwd); single primer covers the mutation.
parameterPanel.strategyOption_partial_title: Gibson assembly style. Forward and reverse primers are independent; overlap is placed upstream of the target codon. Standard for in-house SDM.
parameterPanel.strategyOption_full_title: NEB Q5 SDM kit style. Reverse primer = reverse-complement of forward; a single back-to-back primer pair covers the mutation site.
parameterPanel.polymeraseHelp:
Selects the polymerase preset: the recommended annealing temperature (Ta) rule, the GC range, and the overlap mode.
The design-time Tm formula is fixed (SantaLucia 1998, Benchling scale) and does not follow the polymerase.
Changing the polymerase overwrites the GC range, so re-check it if you set it by hand.
Use 'Custom Polymerase' to define your own Tm targets.
parameterPanel.codonHelp:
Min. changes: fewest nucleotide changes from wild-type codon (minimises synthesis cost).
Optimal: highest-frequency codon for the selected organism (maximises expression).
parameterPanel.codonOption_closest: Min. changes (fewest nt changes from WT)
parameterPanel.codonOption_closest_title: Pick the mutant codon with the fewest nucleotide changes from the wild-type codon. Minimises primer mismatch and synthesis cost.
parameterPanel.codonOption_optimal_title: Pick the highest-frequency codon for the selected organism's codon usage table. Maximises expression but may require more nt changes.
parameterPanel.mutationsHelp:
Number of mutation candidates to load/design.
For EVOLVEpro/Others mode, this is the candidate design count, not a guaranteed final order count.
Final downstream count is determined by included rows.
parameterPanel.mutationCapTitle: Design count limited to one plate of variants
parameterPanel.mutationCapMessage: You entered {{requested}}. A run designs at most {{max}} variants, one plate worth, so the design count has been set to {{max}}. Forward and reverse primers each fill their own plate.
parameterPanel.tmPrimerTitle: Single Tm target. rev = rc(fwd), so both primers share Tm by construction.
parameterPanel.tmTolHelp: Allowed deviation from Tm targets. Cascade stages add delta on top. Recommended 2-5°C.
parameterPanel.gcHelp:
Recommended range: 40–60%.
Primers outside this range receive a penalty score.
Very low GC (<30%) or very high GC (>70%) reduces synthesis quality.
parameterPanel.gcRangeTitle: Recommended range: 40-60%. Primers outside this range receive a penalty.
parameterPanel.gcInvalidError: Min must be less than Max
parameterPanel.primerLenHelp:
KOD One PCR Master Mix
  Standard:     22–35 bp, Tm >63°C
  Long targets: 25–35 bp, Tm >65°C

Experimental (EGFP SDM, demo)
  Forward total: 19–38 bp (incl. overlap)
  Reverse total: 18–32 bp (incl. overlap)

KURO primer length = overlap + priming region
parameterPanel.primerLenSingleTitle: Single length range applies to both primers (rev = rc(fwd)).
parameterPanel.primerLenInvalidError: Min must be less than Max
parameterPanel.autoRescueTitle: When enabled, retries failed mutations through 4 (top-N) or 6 (pipeline) stages of relaxed parameters. When disabled, failed mutations remain as-is with no auto-retry.
parameterPanel.seedTitle: Optional integer seed. Will be passed to the backend and recorded in run manifests once manifest wiring is complete (backend integration pending).
parameterPanel.tmPrimerHelp: Target Tm (°C) for symmetric full-overlap primers. Default 62.

parameterPanel.tmRevHelp: Target Tm (°C) for reverse primer. Should approximate tmFwd for balanced PCR.
parameterPanel.tmOverlapHelp: Target Tm (°C) of the overlap region between two primers.
parameterPanel.gcRangeHelp: Accepted GC content range (%) for primer regions. Recommended 40-60.
parameterPanel.primerLenLimitHelp: Toggle to bound primer length. When off, engine uses Tm-only optimization.
parameterPanel.primerLenFwdHelp: Forward primer length range (nt). Default 17-39 covers most SDM cases.
parameterPanel.autoRescueHelp: Auto-fill failed mutations with relaxed constraints in a second pass.
parameterPanel.seedHelp: Random seed for reproducible primer ranking. Leave empty for auto (time-based).
parameterPanel.tmSectionHelp: Melting temperature targets define how the engine balances primer stability and selectivity.

whatsNewDialog.title: What's New in v{{version}}
whatsNewDialog.descriptionRange: Highlights from every update since v{{from}}.
highlights: Variant names on the analyze plate map now grow with the plate instead of staying at one fixed size.
Expanding the plate makes the writing bigger, not just the cells.
Names that were cut off in a narrow plate become readable once the plate has room.

0.16.15: Variant names on the analyze plate map now grow with the plate instead of staying at one fixed size.
Expanding the plate makes the writing bigger, not just the cells.
Names that were cut off in a narrow plate become readable once the plate has room.
0.16.14: Variant names on the well grid are no longer cut off. Two variants that differ only in the last character can be told apart at a glance.
A name too long for one line wraps inside its cell instead of being truncated.
0.16.13: The well selection panel writes a barcode worklist: every filled well, its barcode, and the two seed primers that make it.
It also states which seeds the campaign actually needs, which for a partly filled plate is fewer than the twenty in the workbook.
The list is built from the same layout the run scores, so it cannot describe a different plate than the one analysed.
Seeds the barcode workbook does not carry are named rather than left blank.
0.16.12: The review screen now names the samples a run left off the plate, instead of leaving them as a blank cell and a missing table row.
That list is read from the finished run, so reopening a project still says what was left out.
Runs that filled every well they drafted are unaffected and show no notice.
0.16.11: Selecting wells no longer moves the variants. Each keeps the well the plate order gave it, and a click only says which wells were filled.
A plate filled only in part now runs. Fewer selected wells than samples used to be refused before the run could start.
Variants in wells left out are named above the grid and struck through in it, so none of them drops out of a run in silence.
The finished run records which wells were left out and what was in them, so a result can say what was never on the plate.
0.16.10: Saving a project on macOS and Linux now works. Autosave was silently refused there, so reopening a project restored nothing.
MAME analyze output and KURO inputs survive a restart on those platforms, the same way they already did on Windows.
The update notes now cover every release between the version you last ran and the one you just installed, not only the newest one.
Each release in that list gets its own heading, and the list scrolls when several releases are shown at once.
0.16.9: One Echo row builder feeds the csv, the xlsx worklist and the preview, so all three name the same source well under a quadrant.
Starting a run without pressing Validate no longer skips the guard against picking the fastq_pass folder instead of the run folder.
The drawer stops reporting a merged row count it never counted, and reopening a project reports recovery instead of n/a.
Files the sidecar accepts are no longer refused by the pickers, and provenance files carry one release version instead of three.
0.16.8: Step 4.2 now receives the wild-type replicates that step 4.1 measured, instead of being told none exist.
A workbook with no wild-type column and one with too few replicates are different answers, and the screen says which it is.
Replicates reach the classifier only when there are enough to estimate assay noise, so no verdict rests on one signal at full confidence.
The backtest that decides which signals drive the advisory is now in the repository, not cited by filename alone.
0.16.7: The final culture plate now lines up with the stock plate it came from, instead of pulling later picks forward into a dropped clone's well.
Packing the final plate from A1 stays available as a layout choice; only the default changed, and a prior choice of it survives the upgrade.
The exported mapping CSV always starts with the header row, instead of a metadata comment line pushing it to row two.
0.16.6: Step 4.2 now distinguishes a verdict it withheld from a question it was never able to ask, and names the input it was missing.
Step 4.2 fills its file list from what each round produced, instead of asking for the file step 4.1 just wrote.
A stored advisory verdict is shown as superseded once its inputs are rebuilt, rather than passing as the current answer.
The step 4.2 completion mark survives a restart instead of appearing only after the screen is opened.
The handoff button on step 4.2 is removed; the step that filled its precondition was taken out in v0.15.12.
0.16.5: The design count stops at 96 variants, one plate worth, and names the refused number instead of accepting a count the plate cannot hold.
A saved project or autosave snapshot carrying a larger count is corrected when it is opened, not rejected.
Well labels past the end of a plate name the next plate, matching what the Python exporter has always produced.
0.16.4: The well selection grid draws the plate again instead of reporting that a sidecar method was not found.
A campaign that occupies part of the plate can declare its wells again, rather than falling back to the leading ones.
0.16.3: The instrument sheet fills the final plate in the same order the step 2.2 plate map reads, instead of by sequencing depth.
The reference sequence field asks for the construct that carries the primer binding regions, which is what the pipeline has always needed.
A run that extracted its amplicon now says so, naming the region it analysed.
The pooled barcode option states that it merges every read in the folder, not only the ticked barcodes.
0.16.2: The bundled sample no longer reports a cross-talk check as clean when that check never ran.
The sample analysis fixture is bundled with the app, so the demo reads it in a released build rather than only in development.
Reopening a saved run brings back its off-layout record count instead of showing nothing.
The recovery bar and the header above it can no longer show figures from two different runs.
The KURO plate preview stops labelling its two panels as deck racks, which are plate names now.
0.16.1: The JANUS mapping file now matches the workbook the lab seeds from: eight columns, with plates named rather than numbered.
Step 3 asks for one transfer volume instead of two, defaulting to the 70 uL this lab uses.
Clicking a replicate in the review inspector opens that copy, the way clicking its well or its table row already did.
Each confidence metric now opens a popup stating what it counts and which threshold, if any, the run was judged against.
Verdict legend entries explain themselves on hover, in your own language, at both places they appear.
0.16.0: The sample map is gone. MAME places the plate from the variant list itself, and a leftover file is compared rather than obeyed.
Pick which wells a run used on a 96 well grid, by clicking, dragging, or clicking a row or column header.
A variant list with a blank row in the middle, or a second wild-type row, stops the run instead of shifting every later well.
Choosing native barcodes now says what it is choosing: replicates of one plate. Wells whose replicates disagree are flagged.
A run reports reads that landed outside the declared wells, split by whether those barcode indices were ever used.
0.15.23: The rule that turns a barcode pair into a plate well lives in one place instead of four, so the four cannot drift apart.
A design that fills the plate exactly, leaving no room for a wild-type well, is no longer refused for it.
Loading a barcode file shows how many forward and reverse barcodes it holds, and how many wells they describe.
The native barcode dialog says what it is choosing: replicates of one plate, rather than separate plates.
A run that overflows the plate is refused before the demux starts, not after wells have been written.
0.15.22: A project only asks to be re-analysed when this version would actually score the run differently, not because the version number moved.
When it does ask, it says which changes make the saved run obsolete, so the hour of re-analysis has a stated reason.
A run scored by another version is no longer shown at all: no verdict table, no plate, no export. There is no "keep these results".
Nothing is deleted. The saved run stays in the project folder, and a re-run replaces it.
0.15.21: The barcode annealing tail is now read from the file itself, so a barcode set designed for any gene gets cut in the right place.
A file whose tail cannot be read stops the run, instead of guessing a cut point and filing reads into wells they do not belong to.
Reverse barcodes no longer lose their last base, which had been narrowing the evidence used to pick a plate row.
The result workbook records which annealing tail was derived, so a finished run can be audited later.
The bundled barcode sample was rebuilt to carry the seed plus shared tail structure the reader expects.
0.15.20: A run restored from an older kuma now says which version scored it, instead of appearing as if this build had just produced it.
You choose what happens next: re-run for a result this build stands behind, or keep the saved one. Nothing is deleted or re-run for you.
Keeping is remembered per project and per version, so the notice stays quiet until a different snapshot turns up.
A snapshot with no recorded version, or one from a newer build, is reported rather than trusted.
0.15.19: A barcode file not numbered for an 8 by 12 plate now stops the run and names the barcodes at fault, instead of leaving wells unnamed.
A gap in the barcode numbering is caught too, which used to shift every later barcode into the wrong row or column.
The plate shape is now stated once instead of being written out at each place that maps a well.
0.15.18: The plate map and the verdict breakdown now draw whole instead of scrolling inside a box far shorter than they need.
Step 2.2 scrolls as one page, so the two of them and the verdict table read in a single pass.
The verdict table keeps its own scroll, bounded to about the height of the two panels beside it.
0.15.17: A well now reports its typical background noise beside its worst position, so the mixed gate can be judged against the run at hand.
On the 260729 run that gate sits about sixty times above a typical position and four times above the noisiest one observed.
0.15.16: What's New now shows a short note per release instead of a cut-off copy of the changelog.
Those notes are translated into all ten languages, and a release cannot ship with a stale one.
The variant mapping help now says which way wells are filled: A1, B1, C1 to H1, then A2.
The post-commit version hook no longer breaks on a path that was removed.
A long release note now scrolls inside the dialog instead of running off the bottom.
